next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Oklahoma State Election Board — Next Election

glance_notes.source_name: Oklahoma State Election Board — 2026 Voter Information Calendar
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: Oklahoma's voter registration deadline for the November 3, 2026 General Election is October 9. Oklahoma does not provide general same-day voter registration.

glance_notes.source_name: Oklahoma State Election Board — 2026 Voter Information Calendar
glance_notes.text: Early Voting October 28–31: For the November 3, 2026 General Election, Oklahoma early voting is available October 28 through October 30 from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. and October 31 from 8:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. No excuse is required.

glance_notes.source_name: Oklahoma State Election Board — Proof of Identity
glance_notes.text: Proof of Identity Required: Oklahoma requires proof of identity for in-person voting. Voters may use qualifying government-issued photo identification or the free voter identification card issued by their County Election Board. A voter without acceptable proof of identity may vote a provisional ballot after signing a sworn affidavit.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Oklahoma residents may register online, in person or by mail. Online registration is available to applicants who have a current and valid Oklahoma driver license or state identification card on file with Service Oklahoma and whose identification address matches the address being used for voter registration. Paper applications may be submitted through County Election Boards and other authorized voter registration agencies. To register, a person must be a U.S. citizen, be at least 18 years old and meet Oklahoma's residency and other eligibility requirements. Eligible 17-and-a-half-year-olds may preregister but cannot vote until age 18. A person convicted of a felony may register after fully serving the sentence ordered by the court, including any required incarceration, probation or parole, or after qualifying for another restoration method recognized by Oklahoma law.
register.source_name: Oklahoma State Election Board — Register to Vote
register.internal_note: The State Election Board confirms online, mail and in-person registration. Online applicants must meet the Oklahoma driver license/state ID requirements. Oklahoma's felony rule should not be simplified to release from incarceration; eligibility generally returns after the entire sentence ordered by the court has been completed, including probation or parole, although pardons and certain commutations can affect eligibility. Persons adjudged incapacitated by a court cannot register, while a partially incapacitated person is not automatically disqualified unless the court order restricts voter registration.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use the OK Voter Portal to confirm your voter registration and review voter-specific election information. The portal can also provide your polling place, sample ballot, absentee-ballot information and voter history. Voters who discover incorrect registration information should contact their County Election Board.
check_registration.glance_value: Check through the OK Voter Portal
check_registration.source_name: Oklahoma State Election Board — OK Voter Portal
check_registration.internal_note: The State Election Board repeatedly directs voters to the OK Voter Portal for registration information, polling places, sample ballots and absentee-ballot tracking. Voter history is manually entered after elections and may take several weeks to appear.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: Oklahoma's voter registration deadline is 25 days before an election. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the deadline is Friday, October 9. Mailed applications must be postmarked by the deadline, and applications delivered in person must be received by the deadline. Applications and qualifying registration changes submitted after the deadline are processed after the election. Oklahoma does not provide general same-day registration during early voting or on Election Day.
deadlines.source_name: Oklahoma State Election Board — 2026 Voter Information Calendar
deadlines.internal_note: The official 2026 Voter Information Calendar directly establishes October 9 as the November General Election registration deadline. The State Election Board's registration guidance confirms the 25-day rule and explains that applications postmarked or received 24 or fewer days before Election Day are processed after that election.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use the OK Voter Portal to find your assigned Election Day polling place. Oklahoma voters must vote at the polling place assigned to their precinct on Election Day. Early voting uses separate designated locations within the voter's county, so an early-voting location may be different from the voter's Election Day polling place. Voters should verify their location before voting because polling places can change.
polling_place.glance_value: Find your assigned polling place in the OK Voter Portal
polling_place.source_name: Oklahoma State Election Board — OK Voter Portal
polling_place.internal_note: The State Election Board explicitly states that voters must vote at their assigned precinct polling place on Election Day. Early voting is county-based and uses designated early-voting sites. The November 2026 polling-place information should be rechecked close to Election Day.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Oklahoma's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. Voters who are in line at 7:00 p.m. may remain in line and vote. Voters must vote at their assigned precinct polling place and must provide proof of identity before receiving an ordinary ballot. A voter who does not have or declines to show acceptable proof of identity may cast a provisional ballot after signing a sworn affidavit.
election_day.source_name: Oklahoma State Election Board — Next Election
election_day.internal_note: The State Election Board's current November 3 election page directly confirms 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. Election Day hours. Oklahoma's election-security and proof-of-identity guidance confirms that Election Day voters use their assigned precinct, show proof of identity and sign the precinct registry. A provisional affidavit process is available when proof of identity is not shown.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Oklahoma polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. A voter who is in line at 7:00 p.m. is entitled to remain in line and vote.
polling_hours.source_name: Oklahoma State Election Board — Dates and Deadlines
polling_hours.internal_note: Oklahoma uses uniform statewide Election Day polling hours of 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. The State Election Board's current FAQ and 2026 election calendar both confirm these hours.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: Oklahoma calls early voting in-person absentee voting, and no excuse is required. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early voting is available Wednesday, October 28 through Friday, October 30 from 8:00 a.m. until 6:00 p.m., and Saturday, October 31 from 8:00 a.m. until 2:00 p.m. Voters must vote early in the county where they are registered. Early-voting locations are designated locally and should be confirmed before voting.
early_voting.source_name: Oklahoma State Election Board — Early Voting
early_voting.internal_note: The State Election Board directly confirms that early voting is available to all voters without an excuse. General Elections include Wednesday early voting in addition to Thursday, Friday and Saturday. The official 2026 calendar establishes October 28-30 from 8:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. and October 31 from 8:00 a.m.-2:00 p.m.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee Voting by Mail
absentee_mail.content: Any registered Oklahoma voter may request an absentee ballot without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, an ordinary absentee-ballot request must be received by the County Election Board no later than 5:00 p.m. Monday, October 19. Mailed absentee ballots must be received by the County Election Board no later than 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. A voter who hand-delivers an absentee ballot to the County Election Board must do so by the close of business on Monday, November 2. Standard absentee-ballot affidavits generally must be notarized, while some special absentee categories use different witnessing requirements. Oklahoma law prohibits unauthorized absentee-ballot harvesting.
absentee_mail.glance_value: No excuse; request by 5:00 p.m. October 19
absentee_mail.source_name: Oklahoma State Election Board — Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.internal_note: The State Election Board directly establishes the third-Monday 5:00 p.m. request deadline, the 7:00 p.m. Election Day receipt deadline for mailed ballots and the close-of-business Monday-before-Election-Day deadline for hand-delivered ballots. For November 3, 2026, those dates are October 19 and November 2. Standard absentee affidavits are notarized; physically incapacitated and some other special categories use two witnesses. Notaries may not charge a fee to notarize an Oklahoma absentee-ballot affidavit.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Oklahoma requires proof of identity for in-person voting, including early voting. A voter may present a document issued by the United States government, the State of Oklahoma or a federally recognized tribal government that contains the voter's name, photograph and an expiration date after Election Day, unless the identification is valid indefinitely. The voter's name must substantially conform to the name in the precinct registry. A voter may alternatively use the free voter identification card issued by the County Election Board even though that card does not contain a photograph. A voter who does not have or refuses to show acceptable proof of identity may cast a provisional ballot after signing a sworn affidavit.
voter_id.glance_value: Proof of identity required; free voter card or provisional option available
voter_id.source_name: Oklahoma State Election Board — Proof of Identity
voter_id.internal_note: Oklahoma's requirement is technically a proof-of-identity law rather than an absolute photo-ID-only requirement. Qualifying federal, Oklahoma or federally recognized tribal photo identification is accepted, but the County Election Board voter identification card is also valid even though it has no photograph. A voter without proof may use a provisional ballot and sworn affidavit; the ballot is counted if required affidavit information matches the voter registration record and other eligibility requirements are met.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Oklahoma provides accessible voting and assistance for voters with disabilities. Voters with visual or physical disabilities may vote privately and independently using accessible voting equipment during Election Day and early voting. A voter who needs assistance because of a disability or inability to read may choose an assistant, except the voter's employer, an agent of the employer or an agent of the voter's union. Voters who cannot enter a polling place because of a physical disability may receive assistance from election officials outside the polling place in qualifying circumstances. Blind voters may also request an accessible absentee ballot through Oklahoma's Electronic Accessible Delivery System, which allows the ballot to be received and marked electronically; the completed ballot must then be printed and returned using the required ballot-return materials.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible equipment, assistance and accessible absentee voting
accessible_voting.source_name: Oklahoma State Election Board — Accessibility for Disabled Voters
accessible_voting.internal_note: Oklahoma's Hart InterCivic eScan A/T includes an audio tactile interface for independent voting and supports compatible sip-and-puff or tactile input devices. Blind voters may use EADS to receive and mark a ballot electronically, but the ballot must be printed and physically returned. This should not be described as general online voting.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Oklahoma provides special voting procedures for eligible uniformed-service members, qualifying spouses and dependents, and U.S. citizens living overseas. Covered voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request absentee ballots. Ballots may be requested for delivery by mail, fax or electronically through Oklahoma's secure Military and Overseas Absentee Balloting system. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the ordinary military and overseas absentee-ballot request deadline is 5:00 p.m. October 19. Ballots for federal and state elections are transmitted no later than 45 days before Election Day. Voted military and overseas ballots may be returned by authorized mail or private delivery methods or by fax and must be received by the County Election Board by 7:00 p.m. Central Time on Election Day.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA and electronic ballot delivery available
military_overseas.source_name: Oklahoma State Election Board — Military and Overseas Voters
military_overseas.internal_note: The State Election Board's July 24, 2026 UOCAVA guidance confirms FPCA use, electronic ballot delivery through MOAB, the 45-day transmission requirement and 7:00 p.m. Election Day receipt deadline. Voters may mark electronically delivered ballots using the MOAB system but must print the ballot and return it by an authorized method; fax return is permitted. The Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot is available as a backup when necessary. Emergency procedures exist for qualifying uniformed-service members deployed after the ordinary request deadline.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in Oklahoma if they meet the state's voter eligibility and residency requirements. A student who establishes an Oklahoma residence for voting purposes may register using that residence, while a student who maintains a qualifying voting residence elsewhere may continue voting under the rules applicable to that residence. Students should register and vote from only one residence for an election. Students voting in person in Oklahoma must comply with the state's proof-of-identity requirement; a college student identification card by itself is not one of the standard forms of proof of identity unless it independently meets the requirements for an identification document issued by an authorized government.
student_voting.glance_value: Students may vote from one qualifying residence
student_voting.source_name: Oklahoma State Election Board — Register to Vote
student_voting.internal_note: Oklahoma's general residency and registration rules apply to college students. The proof-of-identity page limits qualifying photo identification to documents issued by the United States, Oklahoma or a federally recognized tribal government, plus the County Election Board voter identification card. Ordinary college-issued student IDs therefore should not be represented as generally accepted voter ID.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Registered Oklahoma voters can view and download their precinct-specific sample ballot through the OK Voter Portal. The portal also provides the voter's polling place. Because ballot contents depend on the voter's precinct and local contests, voters should use their own voter record to retrieve the ballot that applies to them. The November 3, 2026 General Election sample ballots should be checked again after all ballot preparation is complete.
sample_ballot.glance_value: View your sample ballot in the OK Voter Portal
sample_ballot.source_name: Oklahoma State Election Board — OK Voter Portal
sample_ballot.internal_note: The State Election Board's current Next Election page and 2026 election reminders directly tell voters to use the OK Voter Portal to find their polling place and view a sample ballot for their precinct. Reverify November ballots after final preparation because local races and questions vary by precinct.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Oklahoma State Election Board, 2300 N Lincoln Blvd, Room G28, State Capitol Building, Oklahoma City, OK 73105. Mailing address: PO Box 53156, Oklahoma City, OK 73152-3156. Phone: 405-521-2391. Fax: 405-521-6457. Email: info@elections.ok.gov. Office hours are Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. For voter-specific registration, polling-place, early-voting or absentee-ballot questions, contact the appropriate County Election Board.
contact.source_name: Oklahoma State Election Board — Contact Us
contact.internal_note: The State Election Board's current contact page verifies the physical and mailing addresses, 405-521-2391 phone, 405-521-6457 fax, [info@elections.ok.gov](mailto:info@elections.ok.gov) email and weekday 8:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. office hours. The email address is intentionally plain text with no Markdown or mailto wrapper.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Oklahoma State Election Board website and OK Voter Portal for official statewide election information. These resources provide voter registration, registration lookup, polling places, sample ballots, early-voting information, proof-of-identity requirements, absentee-ballot applications and tracking, military and overseas voting information and County Election Board contacts. Oklahoma's 77 County Election Boards administer voter registration and many local voting functions.
